name: hat_id_eeprom
title: HAT ID EEPROM
purpose: 24LC32A on the Pi's ID pins, as the HAT+ spec asks (address 0x50, write-protected by default)

sources.title: Raspberry Pi HAT+ Specification
sources.licence: Raspberry Pi Ltd documentation; link and quotes only
sources.read: p4 (GPIO2/3 pull-ups), p5 (ID pins), p6-7 (ID EEPROM), p12-13 (power, mechanical)

sources.title: raspberrypi/hats: designguide.md and README.md
sources.licence: Raspberry Pi documentation (repository marked deprecated); link and quotes only

sources.title: Microchip 24AA32A/24LC32A 32K I2C Serial EEPROM (DS21713M)
sources.licence: Microchip datasheet; link and quotes only
sources.read: p1 features and pinout, section 2.4 WP, package codes

parts.quote: "32K I2C Serial EEPROM", "24LC32A 2.5-5.5" V; SOIC pins A0 1, A1 2, A2 3, VSS 4, SDA 5, SCL 6, WP 7, VCC 8 ("VSS 4 5 SDA"); "SN = Plastic SOIC (3.90 mm body), 8-lead". hatplus p7: "Use a 24Cxx 3.3V I2C EEPROM", "Use 16-bit addressable EEPROM", "Use EEPROM with a write protect (WP) pin that protects the entire device memory"; m24lc32a 2.4: WP "If tied to VCC, write operations are inhibited but read operations are not affected"
the spec's example circuit decouples the EEPROM's 3V3 with 100n
"a suitable ID EEPROM attached to the ID_* pins, using 3.9KΩ pull-ups to 3.3V"
"connect the EEPROM write protect pin to a test point on the board pulled-up to 3.3V with a 1KΩ resistor"
"connect the EEPROM write protect pin to a test point" (ground it to program the EEPROM)

layout.rules: hatguide: "Address pins … should be set to make sure the EEPROM I2C address is 0x50. This usually means tying them all to zero." C1 next to VCC.

open_questions: The spec recommends onsemi's CAT24C32 ("This device has an internal pull-down, hence the stiff (1KΩ) pull-up"); its datasheet was blocked. The 24LC32A is used instead: WP whole-array and 16-bit addressing are read in its datasheet; "no clock stretching" is not stated there either way.
An ID EEPROM is recommended, not required, for a Zero-size (uHAT) board (hatguide README: "we strongly encourage this").
